I am a 42-year-old farmer in the South East, and this 0.90-hectare plot is rented, so I am careful about spending too much money on inputs that may not pay back. We get plenty of rain here, and I have grown these tubers—yam and cassava—many times before using the local seed varieties my family has always kept. I will mix some manure and compost into the mounds at planting because that costs me nothing, but I will not buy chemical fertilizer or pesticides for this plot. Between my wife, my children, and myself, we will handle most of the planting, weeding, and harvesting work, though I will hire a few young men from the village for about three to four weeks during the busy harvest season when the labor is heavy.
